title: Envelope
description:
A signed batch as it travels over the wire to `POST /api/v1/ingest`.

The signature is computed over the canonical-JSON (RFC 8785) encoding of
`payload` only, so it verifies independently of how the envelope is framed.

deviceId.description: ULID of the device that produced and signed this batch.

payload.description: The attestation batch being attested to.

ArtifactKind.description: What an artifact ref points at.

ArtifactRef.description: A git artifact the cloud can anchor against (confirm it exists + author matches).

authorEmail.description:
Commit author email — the identity the cloud anchors the commit to.
Optional + omitted-when-absent (keeps the signing vector byte-identical).

authoredAt.description:
RFC 3339 author date of the commit. Lets the cloud anchor an interval to a
commit by author + time without re-reading the remote.
Optional + omitted-when-absent so older payloads (and the signing vector)
stay byte-identical.

blobs.description:
**Squash-resilient session signal.** Per touched path, the git post-image
blob SHA at the session tip — the object id git already stores. A squashed
commit's tree carries the same blob SHA for any file not further modified
during the squash, so blob-set overlap is a robust content-*identity* anchor
the cloud can verify against the remote (which exposes the same blob SHAs).

`blobs` is git's own term (no denylisted token); each entry is a path + an
object id, never file content. Optional + omitted-when-absent.

changeId.description:
`git patch-id --stable` of the commit — a stable hash of the *change* that
survives rebase / amend / cherry-pick (the SHA does not). Lets the cloud
re-anchor work whose original SHA was rewritten out of the remote: it finds
the surviving commit by branch + author + window, then confirms it carries
the same patch-id. Metadata only — never the diff itself.

Serialized as `changeId` on the wire: it is a stable *change identity*, not
a patch/diff — the privacy invariant denylists the `patch` token to keep
content off the wire, and this id (a SHA-1 over the normalized diff) is not
content.
Optional + omitted-when-absent (keeps the signing vector byte-identical).

gitRef.description: e.g. the PR number or branch ref.

linesAdded.description:
2.0: lines the commit added and removed (`git diff --numstat`), counts
only. With the session's `agentLinesAdded` the cloud can estimate how
much of a commit the agent wrote, and must label it an estimate.

sessionChangeId.description:
**Squash-resilient session signal.** `git patch-id --stable` over the
session's *cumulative* diff (`merge-base(upstream, HEAD)..HEAD`), not this
one commit. A squash-merge collapses N commits into one whose combined diff
matches none of the per-commit `changeId`s — but it equals this cumulative
id when the base hasn't moved, so the cloud can re-anchor the squashed
commit by an exact match. Carried per artifact (the commits of a session
share it) so an artifact-only flush still ships it.

Named `sessionChangeId` (not `*PatchId`/`*Diff*`): a stable change identity,
never the diff. Optional + omitted-when-absent (keeps the signing vector
byte-identical).

sha.description: Commit SHA (the thing the cloud confirms in the remote).

sourceSession.description:
The session the daemon observed producing this repo at capture time, IFF
unambiguous. Lets the cloud anchor deterministically instead of guessing.
Optional + omitted-when-absent (keeps the signing vector byte-identical).

touchedPaths.description:
**Squash-resilient session signal.** Repo-relative paths the session changed
across the cumulative range. Survives squash *and* rebase (the squashed
commit touches the union of paths), enabling fuzzy path-set overlap when
`sessionChangeId` misses (base moved / conflict resolution). Paths only —
no file content. Optional + omitted-when-absent.

AttestationBatch.description:
The unit of sync: a collection of settled facts captured locally.

Idempotent by `batchId`; append-only — corrections are *new* batches that
supersede, never mutations of a synced one.

artifacts.description: Git artifacts referenced by intervals, for cloud-side anchoring.

batchId.description: ULID; the idempotency key for ingest.

captureHealth.description:
2.0: capture-health counters since the previous acknowledged batch, so
the cloud can show when a device lost or delayed events. Optional.

chainEpoch.description:
2.0: increments when the chain restarts (a local wipe, a re-link, a key
rotation). The cloud treats `(deviceId, chainEpoch)` as one chain.

client.description: 2.0: the build and platform that produced the batch. Optional.

deviceId.description: ULID of the producing device (matches the envelope).

generatedAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp the batch was assembled.

meetings.description:
2.1: meetings this device detected or the person confirmed (see
[`Meeting`]). Their time rides [`Interval`]s carrying `meetingId`.

prevBatchHash.description:
2.0: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 (JCS) encoding of the
previous acknowledged batch's payload in this epoch; `""` at `seq` 0.
Makes a device's history tamper-evident: a dropped, altered or
reordered batch breaks the chain the cloud recomputes.

seq.description:
2.0: this batch's position in the device's chain, starting at 0 for each
[`Self::chain_epoch`]. It advances only when a batch is acknowledged, so a
retry re-sends the same `seq` (and the same payload, deduplicated by
`batchId`).

tokenUsage.description: Token usage — a sibling metric, never a billing base.

windows.description:
2.1: time ranges whose intervals this batch restates IN FULL for its
device. The cloud replaces the device's claims inside each window even
where the batch sends no interval, so re-decomposing a window down to
nothing (a retracted meeting with no work left) removes the stale claim
(D-0085). Empty means "only where my intervals land", as before.

A window may only come from a builder that read EVERY stored event whose
`at` falls in it (a re-decompose by time, an explicit resync), never
from an ordinary flush: a flush is an event-id slice, and spool replays
insert events with past `at` values, so its time span overlaps minutes
synced in earlier batches. Declaring that span would delete valid claims.
Readers ignore `windows` from a producer older than 2.1. A reader applies
each window to ALL of the device's claims, in every workspace, including
ones where this batch lands no interval: a meeting and the work around it
can route to different workspaces. Producers send meetings only to a
cloud that does so.

oneOf.description: A suggestion from nearby repo work; never billed unless policy allows.

BatchWindow.description: 2.1: a range a batch restates in full (see [`AttestationBatch::windows`]).

BlobRef.description:
One touched path and its git post-image blob SHA — a content-identity pointer
(the object id git stores), never the file's bytes. Part of the squash-resilient
anchoring signals on [`ArtifactRef`].

blob.description: The git blob object id (SHA) for that path at the session tip.

CalendarFacts.description:
2.1: what survives of a matched calendar event after on-device reduction
(DIRASH-0064). No title, attendee or domain.

external.description: Any attendee outside the person's own domains (decided on the device).

seriesKey.description:
Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256(workspace salt, calendar UID): groups a recurring
series across a workspace's members, and reveals nothing about it.

CaptureHealth.description:
2.0: capture-health counters, each a count since the previous acknowledged
batch (DIRASH-0049). All zero is the healthy case.

dropped.description: Hooks lost for good (the spool was unwritable or over its cap).

hookFailures.description: Hook deliveries the shim recorded as failed, when the device knows.

quarantined.description: Sync chunks the cloud rejected repeatedly that the device skipped.

spilled.description: Of those, hooks the daemon itself spilled because its queue was full.

spooled.description:
Hooks that reached the store late, through the on-disk spool (the hook
shim could not reach the daemon, or the daemon's queue was full).

ClientInfo.description: 2.0: the build and platform that produced a batch.

channel.description: The update channel the device follows (`stable`, `prerelease`), when known.

DayRollup.description:
2.0: one device's totals for one UTC day and repo, sent so the cloud can
reconcile its own daily facts and flag drift. A reconciliation check, not a
display source: display buckets come from intervals in the viewer's time
zone. Re-sent with a higher `revision` whenever late data changes the day.

estCostUsd.description: Estimated USD cost from the bundled pricing table. A label, never billed.

intervalCount.description: How many intervals the device holds for this day and repo.

intervalDigest.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the sorted interval ids joined by `\n`.

revision.description: Starts at 0; incremented each time the day's totals change.

workspaceHint.description: The cloud workspace the repo is pinned to, when the device knows it.

DayTokens.description: 2.0: token totals for one model within a [`DayRollup`].

Harness.description:
Which harness produced a session.

`Generic` is a tool piping events through the JSON-lines adapter — distinct
from `Manual` (a human `dira start` dira): these are agent-style events from
an unmodeled harness.

Interval.description:
A de-duplicated, idle-trimmed slice of human-engaged time, attributed to a repo.

`humanSeconds` is the billing base. Project/client grouping is derived in the
cloud from the repo — never frozen here.

humanSeconds.description: De-duplicated human-engaged seconds in this interval.

identityEmail.description: `git config user.email` of the person the work is attributed to.

meetingId.description:
2.1: the [`Meeting`] this interval is a slice of; `activity` is then
`meeting`. The device has already decided, on its own timeline, which
seconds were meeting and which were work, so a reader sums intervals as
before and never adds meeting time twice (DIRASH-0063).

repoCanonical.description: Canonical repo ref, e.g. `github.com/acme/api`. `None` for unresolved dirs.

sourceSession.description: The session this interval was derived from.

Meeting.description:
2.1: a meeting, detected from local device-in-use signals or confirmed by the
person (DIRASH-0060, DIRASH-0062). Content-free by construction (D-0001):
every field is a closed enum, a time, a count bucket, a boolean, a
device-minted id, a reference to the workspace's own entities, or a keyed
hash. There is nowhere for a title, attendee, address, domain or URL to go.

Upserted by `(deviceId, id)`; a higher `version` replaces a lower one, never
the reverse. A retraction is a record with `state: retracted`.

attribution.description: Where the meeting's time belongs, if the device could tell.

calendar.description: Facts reduced from a matched calendar event, if one matched.

engagedDuringMeetingSeconds.description:
Seconds of engaged work the device saw during this meeting. Reported for
the "engaged during meetings" view; never added to any total.

evidence.description: Which signals were seen, for the cloud's assurance display.

id.description: Minted by the daemon at detection; stable across confirm, reassign and retract.

source.description: The evidence family that decided the meeting.

MeetingAttribution.description:
2.1: where a meeting's time belongs, resolved on the device against the
workspace's own directory.

repoCanonical.description: Only for `method: context`: the repo with engaged time around the meeting.

MeetingConfidence.description:
2.1: how sure the device is. Low-confidence runs stay local suggestions and
never cross the wire unconfirmed.

MeetingEvidence.description: 2.1: a signal family that contributed to a meeting.

MeetingSource.description: 2.1: the evidence family that decided a meeting.

oneOf.description: Detected with high confidence and recorded.
Confirmed by the person (a suggestion they accepted, or a recorded meeting they kept).
Withdrawn: its intervals are gone and it no longer counts.

ProviderClass.description:
2.1: the kind of call. Deliberately coarser than the device's app catalogue,
so adding an app never changes the wire. Readers map an unknown value to `other`.

SessionKind.description: How a piece of work was captured. Drives assurance on the cloud side.

oneOf.description: An AI coding harness session (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode).
A manual `dira start` dira (meeting, manual testing, etc.).

SessionRole.description:
What a session does relative to other sessions. Absent for an ordinary
session; only roles that change how the cloud groups work are named.

oneOf.description:
A coordinating session with no repo of its own: Claude Desktop's
scratch-workspace sessions, or a session that spawned others without
ever working from a repo. Its repo-less time is the "orchestration"
bucket — never guessed onto a repo. A session that spawns others from
its own repo is not one: it keeps its `repoCanonical` and heads a run
only because its children name it as their parent.

SessionRollup.description: Per-session rollup. Agent wall-clock sums freely; it is evidence, never billed.

agentWallSeconds.description: Total agent wall-clock seconds observed for this session.

branch.description:
The session branch (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`), if resolved. Lets
the cloud anchor commits on this session to the branch it was worked on.
Optional + omitted-when-absent so older payloads stay byte-identical.

label.description:
Operational tag for a manual session (`--label`), used locally to select/stop
sessions; surfaced read-only in the cloud.
Optional + omitted-when-absent so older payloads stay byte-identical.

note.description:
Free-text human description for a manual session (`dira log`/`invoice`/`start`
`--note`, or the trailing comment). Purely descriptive — the invoice line.
Optional + omitted-when-absent so older payloads stay byte-identical.

parentSession.description:
Harness session id of the orchestrator that spawned this session, when
the producer could link them. An id only — never a title.
Optional + omitted-when-absent so pre-1.6 payloads stay byte-identical.

prompts.description:
Count of human prompts (user_prompt events) observed in this session.
Optional + omitted-when-absent so older payloads stay byte-identical.

repos.description:
Canonical repo refs this session demonstrably touched, sorted and
capped. Set for orchestrators, whose `repoCanonical` stays absent
because no single repo describes them, and (from 1.7) for a session
that spawned others from its own repo, which also keeps its
`repoCanonical`.
Optional + omitted-when-absent so pre-1.6 payloads stay byte-identical.

role.description:
Set for an orchestrating session (see [`SessionRole`]).
Optional + omitted-when-absent so pre-1.6 payloads stay byte-identical.

From 1.7, `role`, `repos` and `workspaceRef` are authoritative on every
rollup: absent means "not set", so a newer rollup that omits one
retracts the value an earlier one sent (a child whose scratch-dir
preamble read as an orchestrator). Before 1.7, absent meant "unknown".

runtime.description:
The cloud runtime the session ran in (`claude-web`, `cursor-cloud`, …),
from `dira_core::runtime::detect`. Absent for local sessions, so the
dashboard can badge cloud-agent work without inferring it from device
labels. Still metadata-only: a runtime name, never content.
Optional + omitted-when-absent so older payloads stay byte-identical.

runtimeSessionRef.description:
The runtime's own session reference (e.g. Claude's remote session id),
letting the dashboard deep-link the harness-side transcript. Only ever
set alongside `runtime`.
Optional + omitted-when-absent so older payloads stay byte-identical.

sessionId.description: Harness session id, or daemon-issued ULID for manual sessions.

spec.description:
The spec slug this session worked under (`openspec:add-csv-import`,
`capture-pipeline`, …) — the slug only, never prose (D-0001). Resolved
producer-side from an explicit `dira start --spec`, an exact `Spec:`
trailer on the session's commits, or an exact branch match; absent when
none applies. Lets the dashboard attribute time, agent share and tokens
per spec. Optional + omitted-when-absent so pre-1.5 payloads stay
byte-identical.

stats.description: 2.0: what happened in the session, as counts (see [`SessionStats`]).

trigger.description:
What started this session when it was a trigger rather than a person
(see [`SessionTrigger`]). Absent means "not started by a trigger, or
unknown". A trigger is never retracted: a newer rollup that omits it
does not clear one an earlier rollup sent.
Optional + omitted-when-absent so pre-1.8 payloads stay byte-identical.

triggerName.description:
The slug of the Claude Desktop scheduled task that started this session
(`dodi-smart-triage-refresh`), only ever set alongside
`trigger = scheduled`. The producer sends it only when it names an
existing directory under `~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/`, so it matches
`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*` and is at most 64 chars. It is a user-chosen
identifier like a branch name, never prompt text, a task description,
a schedule or SKILL.md content (DIRASH-0046, an exception to D-0001
scoped to this verified identifier).
Optional + omitted-when-absent so pre-1.8 payloads stay byte-identical.

workspaceHint.description:
2.0: the cloud workspace the session's repo is pinned to, when the
device knows it (the repo's committed cloud pin). A routing hint the
cloud validates, never trusts; unrelated to the lineage `workspaceRef`.

workspaceRef.description:
Opaque 16-hex digest of the scratch workspace an orchestrator ran in,
so sibling runs from one workspace can be stacked. Never a path.
Optional + omitted-when-absent so pre-1.6 payloads stay byte-identical.

SessionStats.description:
2.0: counts describing what happened in a session. Counts only (D-0001):
tool categories, not tool names or arguments; numbers of lines and files,
never their content or paths. A field the producer did not measure is
omitted, never zero-filled.

agentLinesAdded.description:
Lines the agent's edit/write tools added and removed (counted by the
producer from the tool input, which never leaves the device).

approvalWaitSeconds.description: Seconds between a permission request and the next activity in the session.

filesTouched.description: Distinct files the agent's tools read or wrote.

permissionPrompts.description: Times the harness asked the person for permission.

testRuns.description:
Test runs the agent started through its shell tool, by outcome. Best
effort: classified from the command's leading words and its exit status.

SessionTrigger.description:
What started a session when it was not a person. Absent for an interactive
session, and for one whose origin is unknown.

oneOf.description:
A Claude Desktop scheduled task fired the session. The producer reads
the transcript's first-turn origin metadata (never its content) to
know.

TokenUsage.description: Token usage for a session/turn. Cost is always an estimate, separate from time.

estCostUsd.description: Estimated USD cost from the bundled pricing table. Always a label, never billed.

ToolCalls.description:
2.0: tool calls by category. A tool the producer cannot place is `other`;
MCP tools count as `mcp` without naming the server.
